newsitem.title: USA: SunRiver delaying unit's IPO until 1997.
newsitem.headline: SunRiver delaying unit's IPO until 1997.

text.p: SunRiver Corp said Thursday said it plans to delay the initial public offering of its subsidiary, TradeWave Corp, until 1997.
It originally was to have been held in September.

The company said it is continuing to pursue the initial public offering, but may also consider interim financing alternatives because of what it described as softness in the marketplace for Internet-related stocks.

"We are in active negotiations to secure a private placement to fund TradeWave's current capital needs, thereby enabling us to pursue an initial public offering of TradeWave in 1997," acting President and Chief Executive Leonard Mackenzie said in a statement.
"At this time, we believe that it is in the best interests of the company and our shareholders to defer an IPO of TradeWave until the market is more receptive," he added.
When the offering was announced in early July, the company said it expected to offer about 25 percent of TradeWave's outstanding common stock.
TradeWave provides software to access the World Wide Web and other Internet services.
